text:
Ida Nakamura: Hi all! Im Ida (she/her)  started today on the SDK team. I collect cassette tapes, bike commute rain-or-shine, and Im trying to perfect a 3-minute commute ukulele riff. Excited to meet everyone :wave:
Jon Park: welcome Ida!! cassette collector squad, assemble :cassette: also theres a commuter bike channel with route tips and a spare-pump library if you need tools :bike:
Laila Mensah: hi Ida  welcome!! small heads-up: lunch tomorrow is from a local deli, they use cashews in a couple of salads. Are you allergic? well make sure theres a safe option :salad:
Ida Nakamura: thanks for asking — I am allergic to cashews (anaphylactic), appreciate the check. If possible can we label the safe tray clearly? Ill also bring my own gluten-free sandwich just in case.
Riley Torres: noted — tagging @facilities-bot for allergen labels and to confirm epi-pen details in reception binder
facilities-bot: Allergy log updated: Ida Nakamura (cashew allergy). Alert sticker will be placed on welcome tray. Reception binder contains epi-pen location & emergency contact protocol.
Asha Patel: welcome Ida! we have a tiny cassette swap box in the lounge — been meaning to roll it into a listening party. ukulele commute riff sounds delightful :ukulele:
Ida Nakamura: cassette swap?! yes please. Also slightly weird question: any chance of a quiet corner to practice uke during lunch sometimes? trying not to scare folks but will keep it mellow :)
Jon Park: we have the north alcove with acoustic panels — usually free after 1pm. also tiny jam sessions happen on Fridays at 4pm (bring snacks).
Laila Mensah: logistics: Ill add an "allergens" sticky to the lunch table and leave a note at reception. Also, do you prefer coffee/tea/iced? quick poll: coffee/black tea/matcha/iced
Ida Nakamura: matcha if it's available, otherwise coffee.
Riley Torres: badge & locker update: reception confirmed your badge is ready; temporary locker assigned (basement #12) for bike gear. Ill drop keys at your desk.
Ida Nakamura: amazing, thank you. Bringing a tiny tape for the swap — 90-minute mixtape of 90s indie and city train sounds :smile:
Asha Patel: mixtape = chef's kiss. also FYI we occasionally run a silly commute-karaoke challenge on Slack — very optional but highly meme-y :microphone:
Ida Nakamura: count me in for the meme-y stuff. See you all around the 6th floor :grin:
